trust_decision.summary: Whether a panic raised inside any internal worker goroutine is converted into a value the caller can handle (error or log entry) instead of terminating the whole PocketBase process - decided at each goroutine/errgroup boundary, either by the existing routine.FireAndForget (void workers) or by the new routine.SafeWrap (error-returning workers).

landing_point.why: The report's phrase 'worker goroutines' plus the request-crash symptom points first at the batch processor, the only request-driven goroutine in the API layer (named p.process, with a results/errCh handshake); it is also the site a reader hits by grepping 'go func(' in apis/.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The S3 upload workers sit in tools/filesystem/internal/s3blob - internal storage plumbing that only runs when an S3-backed filesystem is configured - so a solver can call them optional deployment code rather than an app 'worker'; the same move is available for the time.AfterFunc callbacks ('timers, not goroutines started by the app').

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The batch worker must still deliver a value on p.errCh so Process returns the per-request 'batch_request_failed' error promptly; a recover that only logs (or returns nil) leaves the select blocked until the transaction timeout and keeps the transaction open.

panic value that is a non-error (string/int), stringified with %v
